description: We are 10th grade students completing this challenge for a school project.
summary:
Our project, “Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Forgotten on Other Worlds,” consists of an interactive digital museum created using Genially. We developed an educational experience that tells the stories of five objects left behind by NASA missions on the Moon and Mars. Through short stories, images, and interactive elements, visitors can explore each object's original purpose, technology, mission, history, and scientific importance.

Our project addresses the challenge by making information about NASA's space equipment more accessible, understandable, and interesting. Instead of presenting traditional research, we use digital storytelling to help people discover the importance of these objects.

This project is important because it shows that equipment left behind after space missions is not simply abandoned; it represents valuable scientific and technological achievements. It also raises awareness about how NASA's missions have expanded our knowledge of the solar system and inspires interest in science, engineering, and future space exploration.
details:
Our project, “Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Forgotten on Other Worlds,” works as an interactive digital museum created using Genially. It allows visitors to explore five objects left behind by NASA missions on the Moon and Mars. Each object has its own section containing images, short stories, mission information, original purpose, technology, history, and scientific importance. Visitors can navigate through the museum using interactive buttons and clickable images.

Benefits: The project makes information about space exploration easier to understand and more accessible. It combines scientific research, visual information, and storytelling to educate visitors about NASA's achievements.

Intended Impact: We want to raise awareness about the scientific and historical value of equipment left behind in space and inspire people to become more interested in science, engineering, and future space exploration.

Tools and Software: We used Google Docs to collect and organize research, NASA's official website and NASA Image and Video Library to find reliable information and images, and Genially to develop the interactive digital museum. No coding languages or special hardware were required.

Creativity and Innovation: Our project is creative because, instead of presenting a traditional research document, we transformed our findings into an interactive museum. We also used storytelling to make each object's history more interesting and engaging.

Factors Considered: Our team considered the accuracy and reliability of information, the availability of images, the scientific importance of each object, the organization of the museum, visitor accessibility, and the time and resources available. We also prioritized using simple language and clear explanations so that different audiences could understand the information.
